claims.text: The nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst initially has a statistically random atomic distribution.
Ethanol oxidation conditions dynamically restructure the initially random PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
Dynamic restructuring produces locally Pt/Pd-enriched clusters within the predominantly random alloy.
The Pt/Pd-rich clusters function as active ensembles for ethanol oxidation.
Locally concentrated Pt/Pd ensembles lower the activation energy of key ethanol-oxidation steps.
Lowering the activation energy of key oxidation steps increases selectivity toward complete oxidation products.
Pt/Pd-rich ensembles may also increase overall ethanol-oxidation activity.
Under the proposed reaction conditions, operando measurements and simulations will detect the development of Pt/Pd-rich clusters.
Formation of Pt/Pd-rich clusters will correlate with increased ethanol-oxidation selectivity.
Formation of Pt/Pd-rich clusters will correlate with improved overall catalytic performance.
A uniformly random catalyst has lower selectivity than a catalyst containing Pt/Pd-rich ensembles.
A uniformly random catalyst has lower activity because it lacks Pt/Pd-rich active ensembles.
The proposed mechanism applies only in a regime that does not cause full phase segregation or irreversible nanoparticle sintering.
A reaction temperature of approximately 60 degrees Celsius is proposed as a moderate operating condition.
Inhibiting dynamic restructuring should suppress Pt/Pd-rich cluster formation and reduce selectivity or activity relative to a catalyst allowed to restructure.
